source.title: Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Liam Dugan; Callum McDougall; M. Denton; Philip Pham; Christine Kaeser-Chen; Christopher Callison-Burch

page_placements.theme: Residual polysemanticity and context-dependent feature explanations

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests SAE feature recovery and feature-description faithfulness in Gemma-2-2B representations using trained sparse autoencoders and feature-level interventions, rather than testing the original toy-model geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test superposition geometry, competition for representational capacity, or whether polysemanticity indicates superposition. Detector performance tables are not rows because they measure the downstream detection task. Document-level paraphrase attacks are prompted interventions and are not evidence of naturally occurring model behavior; cited findings are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study uses GemmaScope SAEs on Gemma-2-2B as a tool to build interpretable AI-text detectors. It reports only its own pipeline's results: SAE fit diagnostics (L0/FVU) for its fine-tuned SAEs, detector accuracy, and whether auto-interp descriptions predict the detector's logit changes under paraphrase. None of these results is posed as evidence on superposition, feature recovery in LLMs, or whether SAE features are complete or canonical units.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The conclusion itself says SAE-feature classifiers keep the detector's performance and generalization, and that descriptions have high recall and high precision. It adds that base-model SAE classifiers are surprisingly robust detectors, and that detectors rely on very specific tokens and formatting. The recall-bias caveat and the GemmaScope/Gemma-2-2B-only caveat appear in the Limitations section, not the conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains or fine-tunes SAEs on Gemma-2-2B residual-stream activations and evaluates feature descriptions for an AI-text detector; it does not reproduce toy-model superposition experiments or measure overlapping-direction geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and interpretability mask threshold changed feature-level agreement: PRDB correlations exceeded COLING correlations, and masking generally raised correlation, with the BASE-SAE sign agreement on PRDB falling from 92.1% to 89.2%.

fits_no_version.finding: SAEs fit to the detection-fine-tuned model reach lower L0 and FVU than base-model SAEs, yet perform worse downstream. Fine-tuned-model SAE L0 falls with depth, while base-model SAE L0 stays roughly flat across layers (Table 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction/sparsity metrics do not track downstream usefulness of the features, and fine-tuning changes SAE sparsity profiles across depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Auto-interp feature descriptions predict paraphrase-ablation logit effects: ρ=0.69–0.81 on PRDB and 0.36–0.62 on COLING. Agreement rises with auto-interp score.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Auto-interp descriptions of SAE features are causally faithful to a downstream linear head, more so for higher-scoring features.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: Only Gemma-2-2B/GemmaScope is tested. The authors report that auto-interpretation descriptions are biased toward recall and that roughly half of their features did not achieve perfect descriptions, with precision varying. Feature-level intervention results are weaker on COLING than PRDB. The study does not measure feature geometry, canonicality, or stability across models.
record.rows_left_out: None of the directly relevant numeric SAE sparsity/reconstruction results in Appendix A, Table 6, or feature-level faithfulness results in Section 7/Table 3 and Appendix D/Table 10 were omitted. Detector benchmark results were excluded because they measure detection performance rather than the claim versions. Prompted document-level attacks were excluded because they measure induced paraphraser behavior.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
All: no analysis of causes of polysemanticity.
Not posed as a test. SAEs are assumed to recover monosemantic features; no neuron-level spread analysis.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are not tested. Only the faithfulness of descriptions to the detector head is checked.
All: no comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4. The paper takes SAE monosemanticity as background and evaluates its own detector pipeline. The record's V4 and V5 labels are removed because the rows are own-method diagnostics and validations, not tests of the claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The study tests SAE feature extraction on Gemma-2-2B, but does not test whether features are spread across many neurons or generalize to other base models.
The study tests feature-description faithfulness and an aspect of feature-set coverage, but not feature stability across settings or whether SAE features are canonical units.
No comparison of one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features or analysis of feature geometry.

relation.reason: Paraphrase and zero-ablation agreement validates downstream explanation faithfulness, without testing dictionary completeness, stability or canonicity.

tranche.reason: Uses SAE features to construct AI-text detectors and evaluates its own detector and explanation pipeline; these results do not test a superposition claim version.

source_check.notes: All five rows are correctly unlinked to claim versions. The conclusion's precision claim should be read alongside the limitations' explicit warning about recall-biased feature descriptions.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2-2B representations with the tested SAE settings and layers
reader_labels.reason: SAEs produced sparse active-feature sets with reported reconstruction metrics, and the study used their features as described units; see r01-r20. This is evidence only for the tested Gemma-2-2B setup, not for feature spreading across neurons generally.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Paraphrase effects agreed strongly with feature importance, with correlations 0.69–0.81 and 89.2–99.1% sign agreement; see r27-r32. Higher auto-interpretation-score bins also showed higher agreement; see r33-r36.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: COLING feature-level paraphrase tests and the paper's stated auto-interpretation limitation
reader_labels.reason: Agreement on COLING was weaker (correlations 0.36–0.62; see r21-r26), and the authors state that roughly half of their features had recall-biased descriptions with varying precision.
